summary: Submitted a second-scenario check for the already-confirmed requirement c-snapshot-install-commit-context, with preflight returning valid:true. Rationale: both the first artifact and its review recorded as a limitation that the receiver's log was left intact because TrailingLogs was large, so the install's compaction removed nothing; this artifact fixes that by configuring the receiving node with no trailing logs, so the bootstrap entry it holds is really truncated at the snapshot index, while the requirement, the binding for the installSnapshot entry point, the oracle and the observation path are unchanged - which is why no new claim, candidate or binding was submitted and the product is a plain check selecting unit-c-snapshot-install-commit-context with plan check-plan-snapshot-compacted.json and harness check-harness-snapshot-compacted.go. The harness is the first scenario's harness with the receiver's TrailingLogs set to zero: a real single-voter leader commits forty entries and snapshots at index 43, a voter that holds only its bootstrap entry installs exactly that snapshot through the module's own InmemTransport install path, and the harness reports the receiver's commit index, applied index, last index and state against the admitted index; the assertion is the same, commit_index == admit.index, justified because the receiver's own last index is the admitted index inside the prefix. Limitations carried over and adjusted: the observation is a single post-install prefix that does not measure duration in a live cluster, this prefix cannot tell whether the value would differ with entries retained (the first scenario covers that case), and the equality encoding's dependence on the receiver's last index is unchanged. If the runner executes this before the deadline, the next turn should review it to lift the unreviewed-correspondence blocker on this additional witness.
